'''Faith Hope Among’in Osier''' is a [[Demographics of Kenya|Kenyan]] [[Immunology|immunologist]], [[Pediatrics|paediatrician]] and [[Teacher|educator]].

== Education ==
'''Faith Osier''' was born in [[Kenya]] in 1972.<ref name="Albers">{{Cite web|url=https://www.uni-heidelberg.de/presse/meldungen/2016/m20160801_kenyan-scientist-to-do-malaria-research-in-heidelberg.html|title=Kenyan Scientist to Do Malaria Research in Heidelberg - Communications and Marketing - Heidelberg University|last=Albers|first=Jürgen|website=www.uni-heidelberg.de|language=en|access-date=2018-03-27}}</ref> trained the [[University of Nairobi]], where she obtained her [[Bachelor of Medicine, Bachelor of Surgery|MBChB]] degree in 1996. She worked in the Coast General Provincial Hospital for two years, before joining Kilifi District Hospital. She completed a Masters in Human Immunity at the [[University of Liverpool]], where she was awarded a prize for being the best student of the year.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=http://www.academia-net.org/profil/prof-faith-osier/1353588|title=Prof. Faith Osier - AcademiaNet|website=www.academia-net.org|language=en|access-date=2018-03-27}}</ref> In 2008 she earned a PhD from the [[Open University]].<ref name=":0" /> Her thesis was entitled ''Immune responses to polymorphic antigens and protection against severe malaria in Kenyan children'' and was supervised by Kevin Marsh.<ref>{{Cite thesis|last=Among'in|first=Osier, Faith Hope|date=2008|title=Immune responses to polymorphic antigens and protection against severe malaria in Kenyan children.|publisher=Open University|doi=10.21954/ou.ro.0000d571|url=http://ethos.bl.uk/OrderDetails.do?did=1&uin=uk.bl.ethos.489913|type=Ph.D}}{{Dead link|date=July 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> Osier is the current President of the [[International Union of Immunological Societies]], a position she will hold until 2022.

== Career ==
Before moving to the [[United Kingdom|UK]], Osier worked as a [[Physician|Medical Officer]] at [[Kenya Medical Research Institute]] in [[Kilifi]]. She decided to specialise in [[Pediatrics|paediatric medicine]], moved to the [[United Kingdom|UK]] and became a member of the [[Royal College of Paediatrics and Child Health]] UK.<ref name=":0" />

Osier is interested in how people develop a natural immunity to [[malaria]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://www.ndm.ox.ac.uk/kenyan-scientist-wins-top-scientific-prize|title=Kenyan Scientist Wins Top Scientific Prize - Nuffield Department of Medicine|website=www.ndm.ox.ac.uk|access-date=2018-03-27|archive-date=25 May 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200525033346/https://www.ndm.ox.ac.uk/kenyan-scientist-wins-top-scientific-prize|url-status=dead}}</ref> She works with the [[Wellcome Sanger Institute]] and the [[Burnet Institute]].<ref name=":1" /> She believes the antibody-based malaria vaccine could be effective.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=https://www.immunopaedia.org.za/interviews/immunologist-of-the-month-2017/faith-osier-interview/|title=Faith Osier Interview {{!}} Immunopaedia|website=www.immunopaedia.org.za|date=21 December 2016 |language=en|access-date=2018-03-27}}</ref> She holds a [[Wellcome Trust]] fellowship in [[Public health|Public Health]] and [[Tropical medicine|Tropical Medicine]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://kemri-wellcome.org/author/faith/#home|title=Prof. Faith Osier {{!}} Kemri {{!}} Wellcome Trust|website=kemri-wellcome.org|access-date=2018-03-27|archive-date=19 May 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180519044221/http://kemri-wellcome.org/author/faith/#home|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 2014 she won the African Research Leader Award from the [[Medical Research Council (United Kingdom)|Medical Research Council]] and [[Department for International Development]].<ref name=":1" /> She was also awarded the Young African Scientist Award from the [[European Virtual Institute for Malaria Research]]. Osier also won the [[Merle Sande|Merle A Sande]] Health Leadership Award.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.insight.mrc.ac.uk/2014/08/06/faith-and-hope-leading-malaria-research-in-africa/|title=Faith and hope: leading malaria research in Africa - insight|date=2014-08-06|work=insight|access-date=2018-03-27|language=en-US|archive-date=28 March 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180328040932/http://www.insight.mrc.ac.uk/2014/08/06/faith-and-hope-leading-malaria-research-in-africa/|url-status=dead}}</ref> She was awarded the [[Royal Society Pfizer Award]] in 2014.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://healthkenya.co.ke/2014-royal-society-pfizer-award-winner/|title=The 2014 Royal Society Pfizer award winner: Health kenya/ health care kenya/ nutrition kenya|date=2015-01-12|work=Health Kenya|access-date=2018-03-27|language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://royalsociety.org/science-events-and-lectures/2014/10/pfizer-prize-seminar/|title=2014 Royal Society Pfizer Prize Seminar|website=royalsociety.org|language=en-gb|access-date=2018-03-27}}</ref><ref name=":3">{{Cite web|url=https://www.ndm.ox.ac.uk/dr-faith-osier-and-dr-abdisalan-noor-awarded-visiting-professorship-at-oxford|title=Dr. Faith Osier and Dr. Abdisalan Noor awarded visiting professorship at Oxford - Nuffield Department of Medicine|website=www.ndm.ox.ac.uk|access-date=2018-03-27|archive-date=2020-05-25|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200525032840/https://www.ndm.ox.ac.uk/dr-faith-osier-and-dr-abdisalan-noor-awarded-visiting-professorship-at-oxford|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 2016 she won the [[Sofia Kovalevskaya]] prize from the [[Alexander von Humboldt Foundation]], and moved to [[Universitat Heidelberg]] to continue her malaria research.<ref name="Albers"/> Until 2022, Osier was the executive director of the IAVI - Human Immunology Laboratory in London. Ultimately, Osier looks to "eliminate malaria for the health and economic empowerment of Africa".<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://blog.wellcome.ac.uk/2014/08/26/researcher-spotlight-dr-faith-osier/|title=Researcher Spotlight: Dr Faith Osier|date=2014-08-26|work=Wellcome Trust Blog|access-date=2018-03-27|language=en-US|archive-date=28 March 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180328041042/https://blog.wellcome.ac.uk/2014/08/26/researcher-spotlight-dr-faith-osier/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Osier is interested in improving the prospects of African Scientists, and has her own research group in the [[Kilifi County]] District Hospital.<ref name=":3" /> She is concerned about the brain drain out of African universities.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.timeshighereducation.co.uk/news/%E2%80%98shun-mediocrity%E2%80%99-stem-african-brain-drain-universities-told|title='Shun mediocrity' to stem African brain drain, universities told|date=2015-08-05|work=Times Higher Education (THE)|access-date=2018-03-27|language=en|archive-date=10 September 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150910043953/https://www.timeshighereducation.co.uk/news/%E2%80%98shun-mediocrity%E2%80%99-stem-african-brain-drain-universities-told|url-status=dead}}</ref> She is a mentor with Initiative to Develop African Research Leaders.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://ideal.kemri-wellcome.org/team/prof-faith-osier/|title=Prof. Faith Osier - Initiative to Develop African Research Leaders, IDeAL|work=Initiative to Develop African Research Leaders, IDeAL|access-date=2018-03-27|language=en-US}}</ref> Osier is a visiting professor at the University of Oxford, where she works in the Infection Immunology and Translational Medicine group.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.medsci.ox.ac.uk/study/graduateschool/supervisors/fosier|title=Faith Osier — University of Oxford, Medical Sciences Division|website=www.medsci.ox.ac.uk|language=en|access-date=2018-03-27}}</ref> She is on the Council of the Federation of African Immunological Societies.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.faisafrica.com/en/16/governance.html|title=FAIS Africa|website=www.faisafrica.com|language=en-US|access-date=2018-03-27|archive-date=19 July 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180719233340/http://www.faisafrica.com/en/16/governance.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> She is Vice President of the [[International Union of Immunological Societies]].<ref name=":2" /> She was named a [[TED Fellow]] in 2018.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.okayafrica.com/african-innovators-named-2018-ted-fellows/|title=Meet the 5 African Innovators Who've Been Named TED2018 Fellows|date=2018-01-15|work=OkayAfrica|access-date=2018-03-28|language=en}}</ref> Faith is the leader of the [https://www.smartpartnership.net/ SMART (South-south Malaria Antigen Research ParTnership)] network which enhances research capacity by aiding the sharing of samples and resources from longitudinal Malaria cohorts.

In June 2022, Osier was appointed co-director of Imperial College London's Institute of Infection, where she is establishing a malaria research group.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Prof Faith Osier appointed Co-Director of Imperial's Institute of Infection {{!}} Imperial News {{!}} Imperial College London |url=https://www.imperial.ac.uk/news/236815/prof-faith-osier-appointed-codirector-imperials/ |access-date=2022-06-07 |website=Imperial News |date=June 2022 |language=en}}</ref>
